The core is Rust. Each binding exposes the same facade (`ov-core`): `OvClient`, `Account`, `Vault`,
`ServiceAccount`, `SelfHosted`, the records, `OvError` with the same codes, and the crypto, share-link
and TOTP functions. None of them reimplements OPAQUE, keysets or the KDBX merge. A program on any
binding interoperates with the apps.

| Language | Use it for | Binding | Get it | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TypeScript / JavaScript | Web apps, Node, Bun, CLIs | wasm (`bindings/ov-wasm`), wrapped by `@openvireo/sdk` | npm: `@openvireo/sdk` | [SDK docs](/docs/sdk/) |
| Swift | iOS and macOS apps | UniFFI (`bindings/ov-ffi`), module `OpenVireoRustCore` | `cargo xtask xcframework` (the iOS app vendors it) | [`bindings/ov-ffi`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/blob/develop/bindings/ov-ffi/README.md) |
| C++ | Qt and other native desktop code | cxx (`bindings/ov-ffi-cpp`), `<ovcore.h>` | CMake / Corrosion at a pinned commit | [`bindings/ov-ffi-cpp`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/blob/develop/bindings/ov-ffi-cpp/README.md) |
| Python | Scripts, automation, backends | UniFFI (`bindings/ov-ffi`), package `openvireo` | wheels on the GitHub release | [Python](/docs/core/python/) |
| Kotlin / Java | JVM services and tools, Android apps | UniFFI (`bindings/ov-ffi`), package `com.openvireo.core` | GitHub Packages (Maven) | [Kotlin and Java](/docs/core/kotlin-java/) |

Pick the TypeScript SDK if you work in JavaScript. It adds a higher-level API, the `ov` CLI, `ov connect`
and the GitHub Action on top of the core. Use the wasm package (`@openvireo/core-wasm`) directly only for
the low-level calls.

### How they differ {#how-they-differ}

| | TypeScript (wasm) | Swift | C++ | Python | Kotlin / Java |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Async calls | Promises | `async` | blocking (call from a worker thread) | asyncio coroutines | `suspend`; `CompletableFuture` in Java |
| Cancelling | `AbortSignal` | `CancelToken` | `CancelToken` | task cancel or `cancel=CancelToken()` | coroutine cancel or `CancelToken`; `future.cancel` in Java |
| Errors | `OpenVireoError` (`code`) | `OvError` (`code`, `wireCode`) | `ov::Error` (via `ov::call`) | `OvError` (`code`, `wire_code`) | `OvException` (`code`, `wireCode`) |
| Ready-made Host | yes (fetch, IndexedDB or memory) | the app's own | the app's own | `openvireo.hosts` | `com.openvireo.core.hosts` |
| Secrets | linear memory zeroed on free | `Data`, caller wipes | `rust::Vec<uint8_t>`, caller wipes | `bytes`, can't be wiped | `ByteArray`, `fill(0)` |

### The Host {#the-host}

The core does no I/O. Every binding passes in a Host with five parts: an HTTP transport, a secure
store, an offline cache, a clock and a log sink. TLS, proxies, the keychain and logging stay with the
platform. [Architecture](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/blob/develop/docs/architecture.md#the-host) describes the contract. Two rules apply to every
transport: it must not follow redirects, and it must not send or store cookies.

### Versions {#versions}

Every binding is built from the same commit and has the core's version. Until `1.0.0` the API can
change between releases. Pin an exact version.
